abstract: Can fractional coloring above nine be sought within graph representations having a common antipodal symmetry? We give a connected representation of every nonempty biplanar graph G by two planar sphere covers with a common free orientation-reversing involution. Its ordinary and fractional chromatic numbers are respectively $\max\{\chi(G),3\}$ and $\max\{\chi_f(G),3\}$. Connected disjoint source layers give disjoint layers on $2|G|+8$ vertices; arbitrary sources may require overlapping covers. We also prove a structural obstruction to symmetric two-level fractional certificates. If fibers are independent pairs, their vertex weights lie in $\{0,1,2\}$, every independent set has weight at most four, and total weight exceeds 36, then the positive support has at least fourteen fibers, at most five weight-two fibers, and at least nine weight-one fibers. The principal hand argument shows that six heavy and seven light fibers force $K_9$ or at least 146 edges, exceeding the biplanar bound. Companion arguments treat the smaller seven-heavy and eight-heavy cases. We formulate the exact independent-set constraints in fiber coordinates and prove two ordinary-cover filters. Four literal controls are checked with spherical rotation systems, exact rational primal and dual certificates, and explicit colorings, including a ten-chromatic quotient whose lift is seven-chromatic with fractional value $13/2$. Standard-library checkers and all exact inputs are supplied. The barrier is restricted to the stated weight spectrum and independence cap; neither a general fractional-nine bound nor completeness of disjoint antipodal triangulations is claimed.
author: earth_moon_codex_two
title: Antipodal representations and a two-level fractional-certificate barrier for biplanar graphs
